facts.value: Meredith Corporation (NYSE: MDP). What is sold is Meredith holding only its local media group (LMG, 17 TV stations), after spinning off its national media group (NMG) as NMG SpinCo.
Gray Television, Inc., through its subsidiary Gray Hawkeye Stations, Inc. (Merger Sub).

$16.99 per share in cash (amendment of 06/02/2021; EV $2.825B). The original price was $14.51 per share in cash (05/03/2021; EV $2.7B, of which $725M was cash to shareholders after $1.975B net debt stayed with LMG RemainCo). Shareholders also receive one NMG SpinCo share per Meredith share in the spin-off. Under the 10/06/2021 Dotdash (IAC) agreement those shares are to be sold for $42.18 cash each; that deal is not a condition of the Gray merger.
Fall 2019: preliminary talks with a few private equity firms, including Party B, about possible strategic transactions. None went beyond preliminary talks and no transaction resulted (p.58, p.60).
Met (process 1): 17 parties (confidentiality agreements with 17 parties including Gray, p.60)
Yes. Proposals for LMG RemainCo (Meredith after the NMG spin-off) are treated as whole-company bids. Bids for the four select stations (Nov 2020–Jan 2021) are Other-scope.

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices
facts.value: US dollars. LMG bids before signing are stated as enterprise values or EV ranges ($ billions). Party D's bids are cash consideration plus a percentage of a new combined company, with implied cash dividends per share given from 04/29/2021. Per-share cash prices appear only from signing ($14.51) and in Gray's post-signing offers. Station bids are aggregate dollar amounts. Mixed bases: see Q4.
Cooley LLP (Deloitte Tax LLP was tax adviser; regulatory advisers not named)

Meredith first tried to sell four TV stations, and Moelis contacted 20 parties from 11/16/2020, of which 17 signed NDAs. Gray, Party A and Party B also indicated interest in buying all of the LMG station group after a spin-off of NMG. After final station bids in January 2021, the board paused the station sale and ran a final LMG round with Gray and Party B from 03/17/2021, while Party D pressed uninvited Morris Trust proposals. The board judged Gray strongest on 04/23/2021, dropped Party B and signed with Gray on 05/03/2021 at EV $2.7B ($14.51 per share cash plus NMG SpinCo shares). Party D's post-signing proposals led Gray to raise its price through an amendment signed 06/02/2021, at $16.99 per share with a $113M break fee.

cells.Question: Is the sale correctly mapped as one process with three rounds? R1 is the select-station IOI round from 11/16/2020, R2 the second round from 12/21/2020 (final station offers, revised LMG proposals) and R3 the final LMG round from 03/17/2021. Post-signing contests are post.

cells.Why, with page: E5 tests: (a) no; Gray and B stayed in LMG diligence (p.63) and D returned 03/11/2021. (b) No break: no gap of about two months without acquirer contact between 11/16/2020 and 06/02/2021. (c) Not needed. Gaps of about two months or more: Fall 2019–11/16/2020 (before the process) and 06/02/2021–10/06/2021 (after signing; Gray's consent to Dotdash). Next-best alternative: open a round at the 01/28/2021 pivot, since Feb 2021 was an LMG diligence stage (pp.62–63). R2's Finality reflects the station offers called 'final'; the LMG proposals in R2 were preliminary.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Split at 01/28/2021: rows #37–#43 would form a new round 3, and #44–#68 would become round 4. Dating R2 from 01/12/2021 would move #23 to 01/12/2021 and put #24 in round 1. Live-bidder counts at each opening would be unchanged.
